key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: ACUTE onset over hours, may have intermittent episodes if chronic. LOCATION: Right lower quadrant (RLQ) or periumbilical, may become diffuse. DURATION: CONSTANT pain lasting hours. CHARACTER: SHARP, SEVERE, COLICKY pain initially, becoming CONSTANT if ischemia develops. AGGRAVATING: Eating or drinking worsens symptoms. RELIEVING: NOTHING relieves pain. TIMING: Initially INTERMITTENT crampy pain, becomes CONSTANT as ischemia progresses. SEVERITY: 7-10/10, severe. ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS: Severe abdominal distension (dramatic), obstipation (no flatus or stool), nausea and vomiting, tympanic distended abdomen. History of chronic constipation or prior abdominal surgery. KEY POSITIVES: Massive abdominal distension, right lower quadrant (RLQ) tenderness, obstipation, sudden onset. KEY NEGATIVES: Ability to pass flatus or stool makes complete volvulus unlikely.

red_flags: Sudden severe pain with peritonitis - bowel necrosis/perforation, call 911
Fever with severe distension - ischemic bowel
Hypotension or shock - perforation or sepsis, call 911
